name: Memp (Mem^p): Exploring Agent Procedural Memory
authors_affiliation: Runnan Fang, Yuan Liang, Xiaobin Wang, Jialong Wu, Shuofei Qiao, Pengjun Xie, Fei Huang, Huajun Chen, Ningyu Zhang. Affiliations: Zhejiang University; Alibaba Group; State Key Lab. for Novel Software Technology, Nanjing University. (Corresponding author: Ningyu Zhang, ZJU.)
code_url: https://github.com/zjunlp/MemP (MIT License; supports offline and online procedural-memory building; references LangChain and ETO codebases)
task_domain: LLM-agent long-horizon planning, tool-use, and embodied decision-making. Evaluated on long-horizon housework (ALFWorld) and long-term constraint-based information-seeking/planning (TravelPlanner).
problem_setting: Interactive, single-agent, long-horizon task solving modeled as an MDP where the agent invokes tools/actions over many rounds. The work studies how to endow an agent with a learnable, updatable, lifelong PROCEDURAL memory that is distilled from past trajectories and reused on analogous tasks. Setting shifts from parallel/isolated task completion to SEQUENTIAL task completion so the agent can distill and reuse experience. Supervision: benchmark-supplied binary/scalar reward signals R(env, s_T, tau) in [0,1] (gold trajectories from the training set are used offline to seed memory; online setting builds memory from scratch at test time). Both an offline mode (memory built from training-set gold trajectories) and an online mode (memory grown during test-time execution) are supported.
what_is_retrieved: Procedural memory entries distilled from past agent trajectories: (1) full verbatim trajectories ('Trajectory'), (2) high-level script-like abstractions/guidelines ('Script'), and (3) their combination ('Proceduralization' = retrieved trajectories + model-generated high-level script). Retrieved memory is appended as prior context before task execution.
retrieval_grounding: GROWING / episodic memory the agent writes (procedural-memory repository built from the agent's own past trajectories), with an offline-seeded variant; not a static external doc/API corpus. Classified as growing-memory (hybrid offline-seed + online-growth).
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Fixed top-k similarity ranking: at inference the system retrieves the top-k procedural memories whose query/keyword vectors are most cosine-similar to the current task. Not framed as completeness of a minimal needed set; an analysis varies k and shows performance rises then plateaus and finally declines if too many memories are retrieved.
cbr_cycle_coverage: Retrieve: yes; Reuse: yes (append retrieved procedural memory as context / prior knowledge); Revise: yes (the 'Adjustment' update combines an erroneous trajectory with the original memory and revises it in place; reflexion-based error correction); Retain: yes (Build/Update writes distilled memories back into the bank). Effectively [Retrieve, Reuse, Revise, Retain] all present, though not framed as CBR.
explicit_cbr_grounding: False. The paper frames itself around 'procedural memory' (cognitive-science grounding: Cohen & Squire 1980; Gupta & Cohen 2002) and the Build/Retrieve/Update life-cycle, not as case-based reasoning; it does not cite Aamodt & Plaza or Kolodner.
retrieval_unit: Full trajectory (verbatim round-by-round trajectory) and/or workflow-routine/script-like abstraction (distilled step-by-step instructions and higher-level script). Retrieval unit granularity = full trajectory or distilled procedural script (task-level memory entry).
index_source: Growing memory. Offline-induced from gold training-set trajectories (offline mode) AND online/test-time-induced (online mode builds and refreshes memory from test-set task execution every t tasks). Hybrid offline-seed + online-growth construction.
index_structure_topology: Flat vector index (cosine-similarity over embedded keys). Each memory entry is keyed by an embedding (query embedding, keyword/AveFact embedding, or random for the no-key baseline); no graph or hierarchical topology.
retriever_type: Dense (off-the-shelf embedding model phi with cosine similarity). The AveFact variant uses an LLM to extract keywords, then averages keyword-vector similarities. No BM25/sparse retriever (explicitly noted as future/missing in Limitations).
retriever_learning_signal: None (off-the-shelf). Retrieval is fixed cosine-similarity top-k over a pretrained embedding model; the retriever is not trained. Different fixed key-construction strategies (Query vs AveFact vs Random) are compared but no learned retrieval signal or RL policy is used.
query_construction: Two compared key-building strategies: (1) Query = use the task query description as the storage/retrieval key, leveraging semantic similarity of queries; (2) AveFact = an LLM extracts keywords from the task query, then retrieval averages cosine similarity across matched keywords; plus a Random Sample baseline that uses no key. The new-task query is embedded and matched to stored keys.
query_granularity: Task-level (one-shot at t=0): a single retrieval is performed at the start of a new task using the task query/keywords; retrieved memory is appended before execution rather than re-queried per step.
when_to_retrieve: One-shot (retrieval performed once before task execution; retrieved procedural memory is supplied as prior context for the whole task).
retrieval_trigger_signal: Fixed schedule: retrieval is triggered once at task onset (no token-confidence, attention, learned classifier, or reflection-token trigger). Memory UPDATE (a separate operation) is triggered on a fixed schedule (after every t tasks) and on failure (Adjustment).
reranking: None. Retrieval is direct cosine-similarity top-k with no separate reranking stage.
retrieved_context_refinement: Compression/abstraction at BUILD time (trajectories distilled into compact script-like procedural memories), but no post-retrieval rerank/decompose/distractor-filtering at query time. At retrieval time the chosen top-k is appended verbatim (Trajectory) or as script (Script) or both (Proceduralization).
tool_document_engineering: N/A (not a tool-retrieval method; memory entries are trajectories/scripts, not tool docs).
index_content_separation: Partial: a lightweight key (query embedding or AveFact keyword embedding) is separated from the heavier memory content (full trajectory / script) that is loaded on demand after a key match. Not a formal SOP-index-then-content progressive-disclosure scheme.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A (no external tool index or live tool-sync protocol; memory store is internal and refreshed every t tasks in the online setting).
how_retrieved_used: Prompt augmentation / skill reuse: the retrieved procedural memory (trajectory and/or distilled script) is appended to the task as part of the context, serving as prior knowledge to guide the agent (transforming policy pi(a|s) into pi_{m^p}(a|s)).
planning_integration: Retrieve-then-plan / one-shot exemplars at plan time: a similar procedural memory is retrieved once before execution and prepended as prior knowledge; the agent then runs in a ReAct fashion using that procedural memory. Not interleaved per-step, not inside MCTS/tree search.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per-answer / per-task: retrieval is woven in once at the task level (one retrieval per task episode), not per-CoT-step or per-tool-call.
adaptation_mechanism: Verbatim ICL exemplar for the Trajectory/Proceduralization conditions (retrieved trajectory/script injected as context). For UPDATE, execution-feedback-driven revision: the 'Adjustment' strategy combines a failed/erroneous trajectory with the original memory and revises it in place; the best-performing update is reflexion-based (error-correction) revision.
retrieved_item_representation: Two surface forms (and their combination): raw trajectory (verbatim round-by-round) and distilled script/guideline (free-text step-by-step instructions plus higher-level script-like abstraction). Proceduralization injects both concrete trajectory + abstract script.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Spans raw trajectory (Trajectory) to distilled procedural script/workflow (Script), with Proceduralization combining both. Script = higher-level reusable workflow/guideline abstraction; Trajectory = raw demonstration.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Validation update (only successful trajectories are consolidated; failed/redundant/noisy trajectories discarded) and reflexion-based Adjustment (error-correction revision of memory after a failed retrieval-guided execution); dynamic discarding/deprecation of outdated memory. Also notes that retrieving too many memories introduces less-accurate entries and hurts performance, motivating bounded k.
memory_type: Procedural memory (also described as long-term/episodic-refreshed); a skill-library/workflow-like repository of distilled procedures. memory_type = procedural (with skill-library/workflow characteristics).
write_back: True. The Builder B(tau_t, r_t) writes distilled procedural memories (trajectories and/or scripts) into the memory bank Mem; online mode continuously writes/refreshes after every t tasks.
online_growth: True (in the online/test-time mode): the repository grows and is refreshed during deployment after every t test-set tasks via Vanilla/Validation/Adjustment update strategies. The offline mode freezes memory after offline induction from training trajectories.
write_back_trigger: Scheduled (after every t tasks) for Vanilla and Validation updates; on-failure (reflective/error-correction) for Adjustment, which revises memory in place when a retrieved memory leads to a failed execution. Validation writes on-success-only (success-filtered consolidation). So: on-success-and-failure combined across strategies; Validation = success-only, Adjustment = failure-triggered reflective revision.
failure_experience_usage: Both: Validation discards failed/noisy trajectories (success-only consolidation), whereas Adjustment explicitly USES failed trajectories correctively—combining the erroneous trajectory with the original memory and revising it (reflexion-based error correction). So failures are used as corrective signal in the reflexion/Adjustment update.
memory_evolution_update: Stored entries are mutated after writing: the update mechanism U = Add(M_new) (-) Del(M_obs) (+) Update(M_est) supports add (append new), delete/deprecate (forget-prune outdated/obsolete entries), and refine/overwrite (in-place revision via reflexion/Adjustment). Includes dynamic discarding/deprecation and delta/refine-overwrite updates.
retrieval_as_learned_policy: False. Retrieval/case-selection is fixed cosine-similarity top-k (with hand-crafted Query/AveFact keys), not a learned/RL-optimized policy. The MDP framing is for the agent's task policy, not for the retriever; the paper explicitly notes only vector-similarity with manually crafted keys is used.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: Single-agent private memory, BUT supports cross-MODEL transfer: procedural memory built by a stronger model (GPT-4o) is transferred to and reused by a weaker model (Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct), yielding gains. No multi-agent/heterogeneous-framework shared memory.
benchmarks: TravelPlanner (Xie et al., 2024); ALFWorld (Shridhar et al., 2021, with dev and test splits).
benchmark_family: TravelPlanner = planning/tool-use under constraints (long-horizon information-seeking planning); ALFWorld = embodied (text-based household tasks). Families: planning/tool (TravelPlanner) and embodied (ALFWorld).
baselines: No Memory (ReAct-style, no external memory); Build-policy variants Script / Trajectory / Proceduralization; Retrieve-policy variants Random Sample / Key=Query / Key=AveFact; Update variants Vanilla / Validation / Adjustment(reflexion). Cross-method comparison (ALFWorld, GPT-4o) vs ReAct, Expel, and AWM (Agent Workflow Memory).
key_metrics: TravelPlanner: #CS (Commonsense constraint pass rate %), #HC (Hard Constraint pass rate %), Steps (lower better). ALFWorld: Dev success rate (%), Test success rate (%), Steps (lower better). Also token consumption savings. Plus reward gain and step reduction across sequential trajectory groups.
headline_result: On ALFWorld with GPT-4o, the Proceduralization build policy reaches 87.14 (dev) / 77.86 (test) success vs 39.28 / 42.14 for No Memory, while cutting steps from 23.76 to 15.01. On TravelPlanner (GPT-4o) Proceduralization reaches #CS 79.94 vs 71.93 No Memory with steps 14.62 vs 17.84. Memp also beats ReAct, Expel, and AWM on ALFWorld (best dev/test success, fewest steps).
ablations: Build policy ablation (No Memory vs Script vs Trajectory vs Proceduralization across GPT-4o, Claude-3.5-Sonnet, Qwen2.5-72B): Proceduralization best overall; Script generalizes better to ALFWorld test, Trajectory better on dev (similar tasks). Retrieve-key ablation (Random vs Query vs AveFact on TravelPlanner): Query and AveFact both beat Random; AveFact best on most settings. Update-strategy ablation (Vanilla vs Validation vs Adjustment over sequential task groups): reflexion-based Adjustment best, surpassing the second-best by +0.7 points and reducing 14 steps by the final group. Transfer ablation: GPT-4o memory transferred to Qwen2.5-14B raises completion +5% and cuts ~1.6 steps on TravelPlanner. Scaling-k ablation: performance rises then plateaus with more retrieved memories, and declines if too many are retrieved.
evaluation_decoupling: No. Intrinsic retrieval metrics (Recall@k/nDCG) are NOT reported separately; evaluation is end-to-end task metrics (success/constraint pass rates, steps, tokens). Retrieval-strategy quality is judged only via downstream task performance.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Both outcome and process: outcome via success/constraint-pass rates; process/efficiency via step count (Steps) and token consumption, plus per-group reward gain and step reduction over sequential tasks (a case study shows 9 fewer steps and 685 tokens saved). No reasoning-faithfulness metric.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Strong efficiency emphasis: procedural memory reduces step counts (e.g., ALFWorld GPT-4o 23.76 -> 15.01 steps) and token consumption (case study: -9 steps, -685 tokens), eliminating fruitless exploration. Trade-off noted: retrieving too many memories increases context length and injects noisy memories, degrading performance (an optimal k exists).
context_budget_and_selection_count: Fixed-k top-k retrieval appended as context; a scaling analysis varies the number of retrieved procedural memories and finds an upward-then-plateau curve with decline when k is too large (excessive retrieval inflates context length and adds inaccurate entries). No explicit token-budget cap reported beyond this observation.
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A (uses existing benchmarks TravelPlanner and ALFWorld rather than constructing a new one).
builds_on: Procedural-memory / experience-learning agents: Voyager (Wang et al., 2023), AWM / Agent Workflow Memory (Wang et al., 2024b), AutoManual (Chen et al., 2024), Expel; ReAct as the base no-memory agent; cognitive-architecture/memory grounding (Soar, MemoryBank, CoALA cognitive architectures for language agents). MDP formulation (Puterman 1990). Code adapted from LangChain and ETO (uses ETO-provided train-set trajectories).
contrasts_with: Manually engineered / brittle prompt-template procedural knowledge and parameter-entangled skills; coarse memory frameworks (LangGraph/LangChain, AutoGPT, MemoryBank, Soar) that leave memory life-cycle optimization unexamined; prior experience-learning methods with rudimentary merge-only memory updates. Directly compared against ReAct, Expel, and AWM on ALFWorld.
lineage: Group F (decision-making / memory / RL-style experience learning): procedural/experience memory for LLM agents. Positioned as a systematic study elevating procedural memory (Build/Retrieve/Update life-cycle) to a first-class optimization object, extending the Voyager/AWM/AutoManual/Expel line toward learnable, updatable, lifelong, and transferable procedural memory.
